correctness.rationale: Independently enumerated disconnected induced quadruples of the eight-vertex Wagner graph (rim edges and opposite chords): 26 tetrahedral facets; 111 faces including the empty face with nonempty f=(8,28,48,26). Reconstructed the vertex-pivot acyclic matching with 53 pairs, critical cells one vertex, two triangles masks 38/50 and tetra mask 180; topological sort checks all 304 Hasse incidences. Exact algebraic Morse reduction gives integral top attaching vector (-1,1), primitive gcd 1, so the three-cell cancels one of two two-spheres by the integral degree/Hurewicz argument. Independently evaluated the oriented octahedron boundary on vertex pairs (0,1),(2,3),(4,5) with projection (1,0), a primitive generator. Signed simplex Lefschetz traces for rim rotation r and reflection s are both -1 in rank-one H₂; group invariance and rim/chord structural distinction support full D8 character. All mathematical claims are for this single finite graph, no sampled-to-infinite inference.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: the closest published all-n ordinary four-cut Möbius-ladder theorem explicitly assumes n≥5, whereas the Wagner graph is n=4. The theorem’s n=4 formal polynomial is negative and cannot be extended by substitution. Earlier Wagner total three-cut, ordinary three-cut and matching/Morse complex theorems concern different complexes; primary cut-complex works cover distinct squared cycle, squared path or rectangular grid families, not this exceptional Wagner four-cut homotopy and full integral orientation character.
residual_risks: Small exact finite invariant may have unindexed equivalent calculation; a ranked Resultary search cannot prove historical novelty.

value.rationale: The Wagner graph is the smallest Möbius ladder and an exceptional parameter boundary omitted by the natural uniform ordinary four-cut theorem. Its integral S² type, concrete primitive octahedral carrier and nontrivial dihedral orientation character are motivated exact structure, not a random small numerical count; a future Möbius-ladder equivariant classification needs this exceptional base case. This is not a claimed family-wide theorem.

limitations: Graph is precisely the 8-vertex Wagner graph with ordinary cut parameter 4. Homology character is induced action only, not an equivariant homotopy splitting. No n≥5 family theorem asserted.
